release.highlight_1: Home scanning, Join Game scanning, and manual links now use one join flow for both LAN and Relay invitations.
release.highlight_2: Join failures show the full error type, code, cause chain, and available stack while redacting invitation URLs and credentials.
release.highlight_3: Joining blocks interaction immediately; Internet QR codes and links remain valid while the host is online, and all Runtime base packages are aligned.
release.highlight_4: Windows windowed mode now follows the live web cursor, so games can hide it without fullscreen and never inherit a previous game's cursor.
release.highlight_5: Runtime sharing can switch QR codes across multiple LAN addresses, and the main app and Runtime now share one Playmesh loading surface.
release.highlight_6: The source workspace remembers the last valid project per source, while publish-source uploads no longer repeat project semantic validation.
release.highlight_7: Game-package export has moved to the source workspace. Export can save a source package or upload it to publish sources; the app uses the system save or share surface while browsers download directly.
release.highlight_8: The source workspace can export standalone Android ARM64, Android x86_64, or Windows x64 packages from Runtime base packages that are downloaded and verified on demand.

developer.prompt.runtime.gdevelop.title: Playmesh GDevelop AI development context
developer.prompt.runtime.gdevelop.scenes: GDevelop scene index (use the registered scene-list tool to refresh it)
developer.prompt.runtime.gdevelop.toolDe: Before using a business tool, use the details mechanism declared by discovery in the tool index and follow the returned schema exactly. Do not invent tool names or arguments.
developer.prompt.runtime.gdevelop.chatEn: Use the strict root object {"echo":1,"calls":[...]}, for example {"echo":1,"calls":[{"name":"<tool-name>","arguments":{}}]}. A submission has exactly one root-level echo whether calls contains one call or many; call items must not carry echo. The echo must be a positive safe integer. Maintain one monotonically increasing counter for the entire editor session: its first submission may start at 1, then increment for every details-lookup submission and business-operation submission, never reusing a value across turns or after a failure. A tool whose on-demand details declare the event-payload execution binding must carry one complete GDevelopEventPayload 1.0.0 in a sibling eventPayload field; tools without that binding forbid eventPayload. eventPayload is not part of the official EditorFunction arguments. The console validates and locks it with the call before approval. A payload or execution failure is returned directly: there is no later payload submission, correction, or automatic write retry. After playmesh.gdevelop.ai.return-status.v3, first check the root echo beside schemaVersion; if it is missing, mismatched, or duplicated, warn the user and do not treat it as the current submission's result.
developer.prompt.runtime.gdevelop.chatFi: Return one strict structured object with a root echo that is unique and increasing across every turn of the editor session, plus a calls array, ready to paste into the GDevelop Chat Console.
developer.prompt.runtime.gdevelop.agentF: Use the fully trusted root Developer Token only as an Authorization Bearer, include X-Playmesh-AI-Channel: agent, and never write the Token to URLs, cookies, results, logs, or project content.
developer.prompt.runtime.gdevelop.noStor: Asset-store, external URL, official AI, account, and Credits networking are unavailable.
